title: The Concept of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance refers to the psychological discomfort experienced when an individual holds conflicting beliefs, values, or attitudes, or when their actions contradict what they know to be true. This state of inconsistency creates a mental tension that motivates the person to seek resolution and restore internal equilibrium.

To alleviate this uncomfortable tension, individuals are driven to change one of the dissonant elements. The most common routes for reduction involve altering behavior (stopping the conflicting action), modifying the existing belief (adopting a more consonant view), or introducing new cognitions that rationalize the inconsistency, thereby justifying the problematic behavior.

Understanding dissonance is crucial in social psychology because it explains phenomena ranging from commitment bias to post-decision justification. It suggests that rather than simply seeking objective truth, individuals are often motivated by maintaining a coherent and positive self-image.
